title: Wafer-on-edge stack: deposition thickness sets the cell pitch
idea: Inverts 'the array is patterned face-up by lithography.' Deposit ~300 alternating Si/SiO2 (or n+/p) layer pairs, saw the wafer into slabs, rotate each slab 90 degrees and bond its cut edge to a logic wafer, so film thickness rather than EUV sets one cell pitch; only the orthogonal pitch is patterned, by coarse litho on the exposed edge.
why: Litho/capital wall (fact 4): removes EUV from one of the two pitch axes (~10 nm pitch from deposition control); could cut 5-7 EUV layers to ~2-3 and cost/bit ~20-30%.

title: Backside-etched capacitors through thinned wafer free 4F² footprint
idea: Inverts 'the capacitor sits on top of the bitline (COB).' Build vertical-channel transistors and bitlines on the front side, bond to a carrier, thin the wafer to ~1.5 um and etch the capacitors from the back side so they land directly on each transistor's buried drain; capacitor and bitline contact stop competing for the same face.
why: Facts 1 and 4: enables true 4F² (33% less area than 6F²) and lets capacitor height come from a separate backside module instead of a 70:1 front-side etch threaded between contacts.

title: Recirculating vertical bucket-brigade string without cell capacitors
idea: Inverts 'every bit is randomly addressable in place.' A 64-128-gate vertical channel string stores charge packets in potential wells under its gates and clocks them tier-to-tier like a CCD to one sense/regenerate amplifier at the string foot, which rewrites each packet as it recirculates; random access is per string (~30-60 ns) and refresh comes free with circulation.
why: Facts 1-3: 3D with no capacitor and no lateral transistor; density scales with tier count; separate refresh energy folds into the shift itself.

title: Swiss-cheese tiers: stack defective layers, remap holes in base die
idea: Inverts 'every cell in a die must work.' Accept 3D tiers with up to ~5-10% dead cells, map defects at wafer probe into a per-stack CAM/remap table held in the logic base die, and drop per-tier redundancy rows/columns, so tier yields no longer multiply into stack yield.
why: Fact 2: lowers the yield-driven break-even tier count (26+) and recovers ~3-5% redundancy area; makes 100-tier stacks economically yieldable.

title: Pillar-as-page: activation opens one vertical column, not a row
idea: Inverts 'a page is a long horizontal row.' In a 3D array with per-pillar vertical wordlines and per-tier horizontal bitlines, one activation opens exactly one cell on each of 64 tiers, each sensed by its own tier's sense amp, so the activated page is 64 bits (one cache line) instead of 8 kb.
why: Fact 8: removes the 128x overfetch; ~5.9 pJ per useful bit could fall toward ~0.1-0.3 pJ; also confines row-hammer coupling to one pillar.

title: Heterogeneous tier recipes: fat-capacitor base, gain-cell upper tiers
idea: Inverts 'all cells in a stack are identical.' Build the bottom single-crystal tiers as long-retention capacitor cells and the upper, low-thermal-budget tiers as cheap capacitor-free short-retention gain cells used as a hot buffer, with a base-die engine that migrates rows between the two classes over the vertical bitline.
why: Facts 2-3: upper tiers need no capacitor so each costs less, lowering the break-even tier count; refresh effort concentrates on the few hot rows.

title: In-tier thin-film decoders eliminate the 3D wordline staircase
idea: Inverts 'tiers are selected through an edge staircase of contacts.' Each tier carries its own poly-Si TFT tier/row decoder made in the same step as its access devices, and a few vertical broadcast lines carry the tier address, so no staircase etch or per-tier contact is needed.
why: Facts 2 and 7: staircase plus contacts consume ~10-15% area and many masks at 100+ tiers; removing it decouples tier count from staircase area.

title: Self-rolling nanomembrane capacitors instead of etched 70:1 pillars
idea: Inverts 'tall capacitors must be etched downward.' Deposit a flat strained bilayer carrying electrode/dielectric/electrode, undercut a sacrificial layer and let built-in stress roll it into a multi-turn Swiss-roll capacitor standing over its transistor, giving plate area equal to AR>100 from flat films.
why: Fact 1: breaks the capacitor charge wall without high-AR etch; ~2-3x Cs per footprint if roll diameters reach <100 nm.

title: Wavelength-addressed tiers: light pulses replace wordline voltage swings
idea: Inverts 'wordlines are electrical wires.' Give each tier photoconductive access devices whose band gap is tuned by alloy composition, and select a tier by the wavelength launched into an integrated vertical waveguide grid, so only the absorbing tier opens.
why: Facts 7 and 10: removes 3 V wordline CV² and per-tier decoders/staircase; speculative ~5-10x activation-energy gain.

title: Transistorless 1S1C crosspoint: threshold switch guards each capacitor
idea: Inverts 'a DRAM cell needs an access transistor.' Put a volatile ovonic threshold switch in series with a small MIM capacitor at every crosspoint of stackable 4F² line layers; full-select pulses exceed threshold to read/write, half-selected cells stay off, and decks stack like 3D XPoint.
why: Facts 2 and 4: 4F² per deck times N decks with no lateral transistor; OTS off-leakage (~pA) forcing ms-scale refresh is the honest risk.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM: bond whole undiced array wafer onto logic wafer
idea: Inverts 'the die is the product unit.' Hybrid-bond an undiced 300 mm DRAM array wafer face-to-face onto a logic wafer, route around bad reticles in the logic, and ship the bonded pair as a ~2 TB memory slab with no scribe lines, pads, packages or TSVs.
why: Facts 5-6: kills HBM's ~3x area TSV tax and the package, gives ~PB/s internal bandwidth at <1 pJ/bit, and recovers ~10% wafer area lost to scribe and pads.

title: Vertical-bitline triple-tier activation computes majority inside stack
idea: Inverts 'tiers are independent storage whose data must leave the stack.' Open three tiers on a shared vertical bitline at once so charge sharing yields bitwise majority, and copy between tiers by one vertical charge share, so whole-pillar AND/OR/copy/zero never crosses the I/O.
why: Fact 5: bulk operations move zero bits off-stack; ~10-100x energy cut for memset, copy and bitmap workloads.

title: Array-logic-array sandwich: one periphery wafer serves two faces
idea: Inverts 'periphery sits beside or beneath one array.' Hybrid-bond array wafers to both faces of a thinned periphery wafer so each sense amp senses an open bitline above and its reference bitline below, halving periphery per bit and giving a naturally matched reference.
why: Fact 7: the ~49% periphery share can drop to ~25% effective; symmetric above/below bitlines improve noise immunity.

title: Self-timed tiers: replica bitlines replace global worst-case timing
idea: Inverts 'the array runs to one synchronous timing spec.' Each tier/subarray carries a replica bitline whose sense completion fires a ready signal, so fast tiers return data early and slow tiers no longer set tRCD for the whole stack or cause scrap.
why: Facts 2 and 4: tier-to-tier variation in 3D becomes latency variance instead of yield loss; ~15-30% average latency gain and higher stack yield.

title: Per-tier 2T preamp at pillar junction cuts needed charge 5x
idea: Inverts 'bitlines are passive wires to an edge sense amp.' Place a two-transistor gain stage where each tier's short local bitline meets the vertical global bitline, so the storage node drives a gate instead of a long line, letting Cs fall from ~5 fF to ~1 fF.
why: Fact 1: capacitor height/AR can drop ~5x, turning 3D capacitors into flat lateral plates.

title: Nano-MLCC cells: deposited multilayer capacitor with side terminations
idea: Inverts 'capacitor plate area is set by etch depth.' Deposit N alternating electrode/dielectric films, cut cells, and contact alternate electrodes from two side vias like a ceramic MLCC termination, so plate area grows with layer count on a flat footprint.
why: Fact 1: a 10-layer stack gives ~10x plate area per footprint with no high-AR etch; capacitance scales with deposition cycles instead of AR 115.

title: Tape-transferred monolayer MoS2 tiers, 20 nm per tier
idea: Inverts 'tiers must be grown on the wafer they live on.' Grow monolayer MoS2 access-transistor films on separate sapphire carriers by MOCVD and dry-transfer each 0.7 nm channel onto the stack, so 100 tiers fit in ~2 um and the ~1.8 eV gap suppresses the leakage tail.
why: Facts 2-3: thin tiers keep 100+ tier stacks etchable; the wider gap cuts the leakage tail by orders of magnitude and stretches refresh intervals.

title: Woven tiers: alternate bitline direction 90° to dilute row hammer
idea: Inverts 'a row's neighbors are fixed parallel rows.' Rotate line orientation by 90 degrees on alternate tiers so a hammered row's nearest neighbors above and below are orthogonal lines that each share only one cell with it, spreading aggressor coupling over many victims.
why: Fact 9: disturbance per victim per activation drops ~16-64x, lifting the effective hammer threshold well above 1k.

title: Mirror-paired tiers share one bitline and one plate layer
idea: Inverts 'each tier is a complete self-contained layer.' Build tiers as mirror-image pairs flipped about a shared middle bitline film, with each pair's outer plate shared with the next pair, so two tiers need one bitline and one plate film instead of two each.
why: Fact 2: ~25-30% fewer films per tier pair, giving thinner stacks and shorter etches for the same tier count.

title: Pitch-relaxed 30-tier DRAM in existing U.S. 28-65 nm fabs
idea: Inverts 'DRAM density comes from the smallest pitch.' Design a 3D DRAM at ~40 nm pitch (cell ~11x larger than at F=12 nm) with ~30 tiers, so density is bought with deposition and etch steps that mature U.S. logic fabs already own instead of EUV.
why: Fact 4 and U.S. manufacturability: zero EUV, depreciated tools, U.S. capacity in ~2-3 years instead of 5; cost/bit parity if tiers stay cheap.

title: 1T-nC cell: one access transistor, eight plate-addressed capacitors
idea: Inverts 'one transistor serves one capacitor.' Hang n capacitors off a single storage-node transistor, each with its own plate line; pulsing one plate couples only that capacitor's charge onto the node for sensing, as in 1T-nC FeRAM but with linear-dielectric charge.
why: Facts 3-4: transistor count and leakage paths per bit fall ~n-fold; capacitors stacked vertically over one transistor give 3D without lateral transistors.

title: Microfluidic-cooled DRAM tiers keep 32-high stacks at 45 °C
idea: Inverts 'heat must flow down through the stack to one lid.' Etch microchannels into the back side of each thinned DRAM tier and pump dielectric coolant between tiers so retention-critical tiers run ~40 C cooler than in a conventional HBM-style stack.
why: Fact 3: leakage roughly doubles per ~10 C, so ~16x longer retention and much lower refresh power; enables taller stacks.

title: Hexagonal three-axis lattice: select cells by two of three lines
idea: Inverts 'arrays are square grids addressed by row and column.' Pack vertical pillars in a hexagonal lattice crossed by three line directions at 60 degrees and select a cell by coincidence of any two lines, packing ~13% denser and giving a spare addressing path around a broken line.
why: Fact 4: ~3.5F² effective cell without finer litho, plus built-in redundancy against line defects.

title: Rutile TiO2 on MnO2 template replaces Hf/Zr and Ru
idea: Inverts 'high-k capacitors need Hf/Zr oxides on Ru electrodes.' Seed rutile-phase Al-doped TiO2 (k~90-120) on a thin rutile-structured beta-MnO2 template over TiN, so abundant Mn does the templating job RuO2 does today.
why: Fact 1 and scarce resources: reaches the k~70 target, so pillar AR can drop from ~70:1 to ~40:1 with no Hf, Zr or Ru.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as a registration-free capacitor forest
idea: Inverts 'each capacitor must be etched and aligned 1:1 to its transistor.' Anodize an Al film into self-ordered nanopores (AR>100, ~25-40 nm pitch), line them with TiN/Al2O3-TiO2/TiN by ALD, and bond the layer so each landing pad randomly contacts several pores; pad area, not alignment, sets Cs.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR>100 capacitors with no deep plasma etch and no EUV capacitor mask; only Al, O, Ti, N.

title: FeCl3-intercalated graphene buried wordlines replace tungsten
idea: Inverts 'buried wordlines are tungsten.' Grow multilayer graphene in the wordline trench by plasma CVD and intercalate FeCl3 to bring resistivity to a few uOhm-cm, competitive with size-degraded W at 10 nm widths, using only C, Fe and Cl.
why: W chokepoint (China ~80%) and fact 10: removes W from the array; graphene's tunable work function may also lower gate-induced drain leakage.

title: Short wordline segments with bonded local drivers make resistive TiN fine
idea: Inverts 'wordlines need a low-resistivity metal.' Cut every wordline into 32-64-cell segments, each fed by its own driver in the hybrid-bonded logic wafer below, so plain TiN or degenerately doped Si wordlines meet RC targets without W, Co or Ru.
why: Scarce resources and fact 10: removes chokepoint metals by architecture; shorter lines also cut wordline CV² energy ~2-4x.

title: All-silicon tier superlattice isolated by doping-selective porosification
idea: Inverts '3D tiers need Si/SiGe epitaxial superlattices.' Grow alternating p+ and lightly doped Si epi layers, electrochemically convert only the p+ layers to porous Si through slits, then oxidize them into buried oxide, giving stacked single-crystal SOI tiers from Si and B alone.
why: Fact 2: crystalline 3D tiers without Ge or per-tier wafer bonding; one epi run makes dozens of tiers.

title: In/Ga-free ZnMgO:Al BEOL access transistors for stacked arrays
idea: Inverts 'oxide-TFT DRAM needs indium and gallium.' Use Mg-alloyed ZnO (band gap up to ~4 eV, Al-doped contacts) as the BEOL access channel and stack capacitor-cell tiers above the logic at <400 C.
why: Facts 2-3 and In/Ga chokepoints: the wide gap aims for leakage far below the 13 fA tail, stretching refresh toward seconds with abundant elements only.

title: 4H-SiC vertical-pillar DRAM: wide gap kills refresh, shrinks capacitor
idea: Inverts 'DRAM must be built in silicon.' Make 4F² vertical-pillar access transistors and trench capacitors in 4H-SiC (3.26 eV gap), where thermal leakage falls by many orders of magnitude, so retention runs to minutes and Cs can shrink ~10x.
why: Facts 1 and 3: refresh nearly vanishes and capacitor AR collapses from ~70:1 to ~7:1; taps U.S. SiC wafer capacity built for power devices.

title: Sodium beta-alumina double-layer nanocapacitors in flat 3D tiers
idea: Inverts 'cell capacitance comes from a dielectric's permittivity.' Sandwich a 2-3 nm Na-beta-alumina solid electrolyte between TiN electrodes so the electric double layer gives ~20-40 uF/cm², 3-6x a high-k film, allowing flat lateral capacitors in each tier.
why: Facts 1-2: flat capacitors remove the 3D capacitor blocker using Na, Al, O, Ti, N only; ns ion response and self-discharge are the open questions.

title: Cu-Mn self-forming barriers replace TaN in array and bond metal
idea: Inverts 'copper wiring needs a Ta/TaN barrier.' Deposit a Cu-Mn alloy seed so Mn diffuses to the dielectric interface and forms a ~1-2 nm MnSixOy barrier on anneal, used for array bitlines, hybrid-bond pads and stack vias alike.
why: Ta (and Co liner) chokepoints removed; the thinner barrier leaves more Cu cross-section for ~20-30% lower line resistance at 20 nm.

title: Ferroelectric ZnMgO shadow tier lets idle arrays stop refreshing
idea: Inverts 'DRAM must be refreshed while idle.' Pair each DRAM tier with a wurtzite ZnMgO ferroelectric twin tier on the same vertical bitline; when a bank idles, rows copy into the FE tier in parallel and refresh shuts off, restoring on wake, so FE endurance is spent only at idle transitions.
why: Fact 3: idle refresh power (16-33% of idle) falls to near zero without Hf-based HZO.

title: Edge-wired stacks: plated copper down die edges replaces TSVs
idea: Inverts 'vertical signals must pass through the die.' Stack thinned DRAM dies with staggered setbacks and plate or print Cu/Al traces down the stepped edges to the base die, so no TSV keep-out zones or TSV liners are needed.
why: Fact 6: removes much of HBM's TSV area tax and TSV yield loss, using Cu/Al only with no W or Ta.

title: Capacitive tier vias: AC-coupled signaling with no metal plugs
idea: Inverts 'tier-to-tier connections need metal vias (W plugs).' Separate tiers by thin SiN and pass signals through overlapping Al pads acting as ~1-5 fF coupling capacitors driven by pulse-mode transceivers, with power on a few large Al vias.
why: Fact 6 and W chokepoint: no TSVs or W plugs, and tiers bond without fine metal-to-metal alignment.

title: Laser-crystallized silicon tiers stacked in BEOL above logic
idea: Inverts 'crystalline access transistors require front-end epitaxy.' Deposit amorphous Si on each tier and crystallize it with an excimer-laser super-lateral-growth pulse whose heat stays in the top ~100 nm, building dozens of near-crystalline Si access-transistor tiers over finished logic with Si only.
why: Facts 2 and 7: array tiers over the periphery with no In/Ga oxides, using display-industry laser tools and no EUV.

title: Plate-pulsed sensing doubles signal so low-k capacitors suffice
idea: Inverts 'the capacitor plate is a static common electrode.' Segment the plate per sub-array row and pulse it during sensing so stored charge is pumped onto the bitline with ~2x signal, letting abundant-element dielectrics (Al2O3/TiO2 laminates, k~30-40) meet sense margin with ~half the Cs.
why: Fact 1 under the constraint: compensates by architecture for losing Hf/Zr/Ru high-k; Cs requirement drops ~2x.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM: shrink capacitors 10x since leakage vanishes
idea: Inverts 'DRAM runs at room temperature.' Operate memory slabs at 77 K in LN2 made from air on site (no helium), where junction and subthreshold leakage collapse, so capacitors can be ~10x smaller (AR ~7:1) and refresh essentially stops.
why: Facts 1 and 3 plus the helium chokepoint: refresh power ~0 and the capacitor wall removed; cryocooler power of ~10x the heat removed is the honest cost.

title: One Czochralski boule, fifty tiers: repeated hydrogen-cut exfoliation
idea: Inverts 'each stacked tier consumes a wafer.' Split ~100 nm single-crystal Si films from one donor wafer again and again by hydrogen implant and cleave, re-polishing between cuts, so a single crucible-grown wafer supplies ~50 tiers.
why: Quartz-crucible chokepoint: ~50x less CZ silicon (and Spruce Pine quartz) per tier, using only Si and H.

title: Cu2O/ZnO all-oxide CMOS periphery tier above the array
idea: Inverts 'sense amps and decoders must be silicon CMOS under the array.' Build complementary oxide transistors (p-type Cu2O, n-type ZnO:Al) in a BEOL tier over the cell field to hold local sense amps and decoders, freeing the silicon below for more array.
why: Fact 7: moves part of the ~49% periphery off the silicon footprint using abundant Cu, Zn, O and Al.

title: Copper-catalyzed MacEtch drills 100:1 holes without plasma tools
idea: Inverts 'high-aspect-ratio holes need plasma etch with W or carbon hard masks.' Use metal-assisted chemical etching with a patterned Cu catalyst in HF/H2O2 so silicon dissolves only beneath the catalyst, driving vertical holes and pillars past 100:1 at room temperature.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR 115 becomes reachable on a wet bench instead of ~$10M etch tools, using Cu, H, F and O.

title: Buried back-gate plane per tier: negative hold bias, low-swing wordlines
idea: Inverts 'the access transistor threshold is fixed.' Give every tier a doped-Si back-gate plane under its channels, biased strongly negative during hold to raise Vt and crush leakage, then relaxed per bank on access, so wordlines swing ~1.5 V instead of ~3 V.
why: Facts 3 and 10: leakage tail cut ~10-100x and wordline CV² energy ~4x lower, with Si only.

title: Nanoimprint-patterned array tiers: templates replace EUV exposures
idea: Inverts 'DRAM pitch requires EUV.' Pattern the repetitive cell-field layers of each tier by nanoimprint lithography with C/H/O/Si resists and silica templates, keeping optical litho only for the irregular periphery.
why: Fact 4 and the EUV single-supplier chokepoint: removes 5-7 EUV layers from the array and cuts litho capex per wafer ~50%+.

title: Open standard periphery-free array tier any mature fab can build
idea: Inverts 'one company makes the whole DRAM stack.' Publish an open spec for an array-only tier (bond-pad map, electrical rules, materials limited to Si, Al, Ti, N, O and Cu-Mn) so many small fabs supply interchangeable tiers to independent stacking houses.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital intensity: spreads the $15B fab across many existing sites; supplier diversity lowers chokepoint risk.

title: Fe/MgO/Fe junctions pinned by FeMn: chokepoint-free MRAM cells
idea: Inverts 'STT-MRAM needs Co, Ta, W, Ru and Pt.' Build stacked MTJs as TiN seed / FeMn antiferromagnet pin / Fe / MgO / Fe free layer / TiN cap, reviving the original high-TMR Fe/MgO/Fe system in place of CoFeB, Ta, W and Ru synthetic antiferromagnets.
why: Scarce resources: removes chokepoint metals from a ~10-30 ns, high-endurance cell and may lower stack cost.

title: Hydrogen backside gas replaces helium in cryo-etch of 3D stacks
idea: Inverts 'wafer chucks need helium backside cooling.' Use low-pressure H2 (higher thermal conductivity than He) as the backside heat-transfer gas for cryogenic high-aspect-ratio etch of 100+ tier stacks, with leak-tight chucks and point-of-use electrolytic H2.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline): keeps 3D-stack etch running with no He; cryo etch is what makes 100+ tiers etchable.
